tags: self_ref_fk
description: Self-referencing FK on billing_frequency (parent_billing_frequency_id)

Indicates whether billing is triggered on the subscriber's or contract's anniversary date rather than a fixed calendar date. True = anniversary-based; False = fixed calendar date. Common for subscriber and syndication license billing.

The primary billing category for which this frequency is used: 'subscriber' (consumer subscription invoices), 'advertising' (ad billing via Wide Orbit), 'carriage_fee' (MVPD/cable operator carriage), 'syndication' (content syndication license fees), or 'license' (general licensing). Supports domain-specific billing workflows.

Indicates whether subscriptions or contracts using this billing frequency automatically renew at the end of each billing period without requiring explicit customer action. True = auto-renews; False = requires manual renewal.

The day of the month on which invoices are generated for this billing frequency (1–28 to avoid month-end ambiguity, or 31 to indicate end-of-month). Null for non-monthly frequencies or anniversary-date billing.
For weekly or bi-weekly billing frequencies, the day of the week on which invoices are generated. Null for non-weekly frequencies.

Short, machine-readable code uniquely identifying the billing frequency (e.g., MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, ANNUAL, WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, SEMI_ANNUAL). Used as a stable external reference key in integrations with Zuora, Wide Orbit, and SAP S/4HANA.

Detailed narrative description of the billing frequency, including business rules, applicable product lines, and any special conditions (e.g., 'Billed once per calendar month on the subscriber anniversary date').
Human-readable display name for the billing frequency (e.g., 'Monthly', 'Quarterly', 'Annual', 'Weekly'). Displayed in subscriber portals, invoices, and sales proposals.

Lifecycle status of the billing frequency record: 'active' (available for assignment to new accounts/contracts), 'inactive' (temporarily disabled), or 'deprecated' (no longer available for new assignments but retained for historical records).
The corresponding frequency code or identifier in the source billing system (Zuora, Wide Orbit, or SAP S/4HANA) to enable cross-system reconciliation and integration mapping.

Indicates whether multiple charges within the same billing period should be consolidated into a single invoice for this frequency. True = consolidate; False = generate separate invoices per charge. Reduces invoice volume for high-frequency ad billing.
The UTC timestamp when this billing frequency record was first created in the system. Supports medallion bronze-to-silver lineage tracing per VREQ-035 cross-domain timestamp standard.
The default ISO 4217 three-letter currency code associated with this billing frequency (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Used when no currency is explicitly specified on the billing account or contract.

Reference code identifying the dunning (collections escalation) profile applied to overdue invoices under this billing frequency. Maps to the dunning configuration in SAP S/4HANA or Zuora (e.g., STANDARD_DUNNING, CARRIAGE_DUNNING).
The calendar date after which this billing frequency definition is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended (indefinitely active) frequency. Used for temporal versioning and sunset planning.
The calendar date from which this billing frequency definition is valid and available for use. Supports temporal versioning of billing configurations.

Indicates whether invoices for this billing frequency are delivered electronically (e-invoice / EDI) by default. True = electronic delivery; False = paper or manual delivery. Supports PCI DSS and paperless billing compliance.

Broad classification of the billing cadence pattern: 'recurring' (regular periodic billing), 'one_time' (single charge), 'usage_based' (metered/consumption billing), or 'milestone' (event-triggered billing). Drives revenue recognition treatment under ASC 606.
Number of additional days beyond the payment due date before a late payment penalty or service suspension is triggered. Supports subscriber retention and dispute resolution workflows.
Number of days before the billing period start date that the invoice is generated and dispatched to the customer. Supports cash flow planning and accounts receivable lead time management.
Indicates whether a late payment fee is assessed when payment is not received within the grace period. True = late fee applies; False = no late fee for this frequency.
The percentage rate applied to the overdue invoice balance to calculate the late payment fee (e.g., 0.0150 = 1.5% per month). Null when late_fee_applicable_flag is False.
The minimum invoice amount that must be generated for this billing frequency. Invoices below this threshold may be held, combined, or waived per business rules. Expressed in the default currency.

Number of days from invoice date by which payment is due (e.g., Net 30 = 30). Defines the standard payment terms associated with this billing frequency. Used in accounts receivable aging and dispute management.
The number of period_unit intervals that constitute one complete billing cycle (e.g., 1 for monthly, 3 for quarterly, 12 for annual). Must be a positive integer.

The unit of time that defines one billing period (e.g., 'day', 'week', 'month', 'quarter', 'year'). Combined with period_count to derive the full billing interval (e.g., period_count=3, period_unit='month' = quarterly billing).

Defines how partial-period charges are calculated when a subscription starts or ends mid-cycle: 'daily' (charge proportional to days used), 'full_period' (charge full period regardless), or 'none' (no proration applied). Impacts revenue recognition under ASC 606.

The ASC 606 / IFRS 15 revenue recognition method associated with this billing frequency: 'straight_line' (ratably over the period), 'event_based' (at point of delivery), 'usage_based' (as consumed), or 'milestone_based' (upon milestone completion). Drives financial posting in SAP S/4HANA.
Numeric value controlling the display sequence of billing frequency options in subscriber portals, sales proposal tools, and billing configuration UIs. Lower values appear first.

The native primary key or unique identifier of this billing frequency record in the originating source system (Zuora, Wide Orbit, or SAP S/4HANA). Enables cross-system reconciliation and lineage tracing per VREQ-035.

The operational system of record from which this billing frequency definition originates: 'zuora' (subscription billing), 'wide_orbit' (advertising billing), 'sap_s4hana' (financial/carriage billing), or 'internal' (manually defined). Supports medallion lineage tracing per VREQ-035.

Indicates whether the billed amount for this frequency includes applicable taxes (tax-inclusive pricing) or whether taxes are added on top of the base amount (tax-exclusive). Impacts invoice presentation and revenue recognition.
The UTC timestamp when this billing frequency record was last modified. Supports change data capture (CDC) and medallion silver-layer incremental processing per VREQ-035.

tags: self_ref_fk
description: Self-referencing FK on revenue_recognition_rule (superseded_revenue_recognition_rule_id)

The revenue accounting standard under which this rule is defined: ASC_606 (US GAAP), IFRS_15 (international), ASC_605 (legacy pre-606 standard, for historical rules), both (dual-reporting entities). Determines which financial reporting framework governs recognition timing and disclosure.

Method used to allocate transaction price to performance obligations when a contract contains multiple obligations: standalone_selling_price (SSP-based), residual (residual approach), adjusted_market (adjusted market assessment), expected_cost_plus (expected cost plus margin), equal_allocation (equal split). Required for multi-element arrangements common in bundled subscription+advertising deals.

Specifies the billing product type(s) to which this rule applies (e.g., 'linear_spot_ad', 'digital_preroll', 'mvpd_subscription', 'carriage_fee', 'syndication_license'). Used by Zuora and Wide Orbit to auto-assign recognition rules to new contracts. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_spot_ad|digital_preroll|mvpd_subscription|carriage_fee|syndication_license|vod_subscription|avod_impression|makegood — promote to reference product]

The specific revenue stream or business unit this rule governs (e.g., 'Network TV Advertising', 'Cable Affiliate Fees', 'Streaming SVOD', 'Streaming AVOD/FAST', 'Content Syndication'). Supports segment-level revenue reporting required under ASC 280 and IFRS 8. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: network_tv_advertising|cable_affiliate_fees|streaming_svod|streaming_avod_fast|content_syndication|digital_advertising|international_licensing — promote to reference product]

Indicates whether application of this rule to a new contract requires explicit finance/accounting approval (True) before revenue can be recognized, or whether it can be auto-applied by the billing system (False). High-value or complex arrangements typically require approval.

The contract value threshold (in currency_code) above which explicit finance approval is required before this rule is applied. Contracts at or below this amount may be auto-approved. NULL if approval_required_flag is False.

Indicates whether contracts governed by this rule include audience delivery guarantees (True) — common in upfront and scatter advertising deals — or not (False). When True, variable consideration constraints and makegood provisions must be applied to the recognized revenue amount.

The percentage of estimated variable consideration that may be recognized without a significant revenue reversal risk, expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00). Used when variable_consideration_method is 'constrained'. For example, 80.00 means only 80% of estimated bonus revenue is recognized until the constraint is lifted.

Defines how contract modifications (e.g., upfront deal amendments, carriage fee renegotiations) are accounted for: prospective (treat as new contract going forward), cumulative_catch_up (adjust cumulative revenue recognized), separate_contract (treat modification as a separate contract). Aligns with ASC 606-10-25-12.

The timestamp when this revenue recognition rule record was first created in the enterprise data model. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports medallion-layer lineage tracing per VREQ-035.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to this rule (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Rules may be currency-specific for international carriage fee and syndication licensing arrangements. Defaults to USD for domestic US broadcasting operations.

Specifies how deferred revenue is released to earned revenue over time: straight_line (equal amounts per period), units_of_delivery (proportional to units delivered, e.g., episodes aired), proportional_performance (based on effort/cost incurred), none (no deferral — immediate recognition). Drives deferred revenue balance calculations in SAP S/4HANA.

The date after which this rule is no longer applicable to new contracts. NULL for open-ended rules. When populated, the rule is superseded by a replacement rule on this date. Existing contracts continue to use the rule until their term ends.

The date from which this revenue recognition rule is effective and may be applied to new contracts. Rules are date-effective to support accounting standard transitions (e.g., ASC 605 to ASC 606 transition date of 2018-01-01 for calendar-year public companies).

Reference number or memo identifier from the external auditor's workpapers or technical accounting memo that supports the accounting treatment defined by this rule. Provides linkage between the data model and audit documentation for SEC reporting and Big 4 audit support.

The SAP S/4HANA GL account code for contract assets (unbilled receivables) where revenue has been recognized but not yet invoiced. Applicable for milestone-based content delivery deals where recognition precedes billing.

The SAP S/4HANA General Ledger account code for the deferred (unearned) revenue liability balance associated with this rule (e.g., 2300000). Used to track contract liabilities on the balance sheet until performance obligations are satisfied.

The SAP S/4HANA General Ledger account code to which recognized revenue is posted under this rule (e.g., 4100000 for subscription revenue, 4200000 for advertising revenue). Ensures correct financial statement classification and segment reporting.

The date on which this revenue recognition rule was last reviewed by the accounting policy team for continued appropriateness and compliance with current accounting standards. Supports SOX control evidence and audit trail requirements.

For IP licensing revenue (content, format, music sync): right_to_use (point-in-time recognition — licensee has right to use IP as it exists at grant date), right_to_access (over-time recognition — licensee has right to access IP throughout license period), none (not an IP license arrangement). Directly determines recognition timing per ASC 606-10-55-58.

Indicates whether revenue recognized under this rule is subject to makegood obligations (True) or not (False). Makegoods are compensatory ad units issued when audience delivery guarantees are not met. When True, recognized revenue may be subject to reversal or offset upon makegood issuance.

The maximum contract duration in days for which this rule is applicable. NULL indicates no upper bound. Used to scope rules to short-term spot advertising (e.g., ≤1 day) vs. long-term carriage fee agreements (e.g., up to 1825 days / 5 years).

The maximum contract or transaction value (in the rule's currency) for which this recognition rule is applicable. Contracts above this threshold may require escalated review or a different rule. NULL indicates no upper bound.

The minimum contract duration in days for which this rule is applicable. For example, a ratable subscription rule may require a minimum 30-day term. Contracts shorter than this threshold may use a different recognition approach.

The minimum contract or transaction value (in the rule's currency) for which this recognition rule is applicable. Contracts below this threshold may be subject to a simplified recognition approach or a different rule. Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code.

Indicates whether this rule applies to contracts with multiple performance obligations (True) — such as bundled subscription + premium content + advertising packages — requiring transaction price allocation, or single-element contracts (False).
The date by which this rule must next be reviewed by the accounting policy team. Typically set annually or upon material changes to the underlying business arrangement or accounting standards.

Identifies the ASC 606 / IFRS 15 performance obligation structure: single (one distinct obligation), series (series of distinct goods/services), bundle (combined obligations), license (IP license), service (ongoing service). Determines how transaction price is allocated and when revenue is recognized.

The name or identifier of the finance/accounting team or individual responsible for maintaining this rule (e.g., 'VP Revenue Accounting', 'Corporate Controller'). Used for governance and SOX control ownership documentation.

Identifies any ASC 606 / IFRS 15 practical expedient elected for this rule: right_to_invoice (recognize revenue equal to amount invoiced when right to invoice corresponds to performance), portfolio (apply to portfolio of contracts with similar characteristics), financing_component (ignore financing component when contract term ≤ 12 months), none. Reduces complexity for high-volume advertising billing.

Indicates whether the entity acts as principal (recognizes gross revenue) or agent (recognizes net revenue/commission) for transactions governed by this rule. Critical for advertising representation arrangements, content distribution deals, and affiliate fee pass-through scenarios.

The unit of time or delivery over which revenue is spread when using ratable or units-of-delivery deferral: day, week, month, quarter, year, episode (for content licensing), impression (for digital/AVOD advertising). Determines the granularity of revenue schedule entries.

The specific business event that triggers revenue recognition under this rule: broadcast_date (ad spot airs), invoice_date (billing cycle close), contract_start (subscription activation), delivery_confirmation (content asset delivered), milestone_completion (production milestone met), period_end (calendar/fiscal period close). Mapped to Wide Orbit and Zuora event hooks.

Indicates whether this rule requires documented standalone selling price (SSP) analysis for transaction price allocation (True) or not (False). Required for bundled deals where observable SSP is not directly available and must be estimated.

Indicates whether retroactive revenue adjustments (catch-up entries) are permitted under this rule (True) — applicable for cumulative catch-up contract modifications and variable consideration true-ups — or whether only prospective adjustments are allowed (False).

Broad revenue stream category to which this rule applies: subscription (MVPD/OTT subscriber fees), advertising (spot, scatter, upfront), carriage_fee (affiliate/retransmission consent fees), syndication (content licensing to third parties), licensing (music sync, format rights), makegood (compensatory ad units), other. Drives revenue line reporting in SAP S/4HANA.

The frequency at which revenue schedule entries are generated for contracts governed by this rule: daily (AVOD impression-level), weekly, monthly (standard subscription), quarterly (carriage fee), annually (annual license), per_episode (content syndication), per_impression (programmatic digital), one_time (spot ad). Drives the revenue waterfall schedule in SAP S/4HANA RAR.

Short, externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this rule (e.g., RR-SUB-001, RR-ADV-SPOT). Used as a stable business key referenced by billing systems such as Zuora and SAP S/4HANA revenue accounting modules.
Detailed narrative describing the business logic, conditions, and accounting treatment applied by this rule. Supports auditor review and finance team documentation requirements.

Human-readable name of the revenue recognition rule (e.g., 'Subscription Straight-Line Monthly', 'Spot Ad Broadcast Date Recognition'). Displayed in SAP S/4HANA revenue accounting and Zuora billing dashboards.

Timestamp when this sales channel record was first created in the data platform (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Part of the standardised cross-domain audit trail per VREQ-035 to support medallion bronze→silver→gold lineage tracing.

Name of the operational system of record from which this sales channel record was sourced (e.g., 'Salesforce Media Cloud', 'WideOrbit', 'Operative.One'). Supports medallion bronze→silver→gold lineage tracing per VREQ-035 cross-domain timestamp/lineage standard.

Timestamp when this sales channel record was last modified in the data platform (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Part of the standardised cross-domain audit trail per VREQ-035 to support change detection and incremental processing in the medallion architecture.

Indicates whether AI-generated advertising content disclosure is required for ads placed through this channel, per FCC AI ad disclosure rules and EU AI Act requirements. When True, triggers C2PA/generative-AI content provenance flagging in the content_provenance workflow.

Indicates whether this sales channel supports audience-guaranteed deals (True), where delivery is guaranteed against a demographic target (e.g., Adults 18-49 GRP guarantee). Relevant for upfront and scatter TV sales with Nielsen or Comscore measurement.

Name of the system that provides inventory availability (avails) data for this sales channel (e.g., 'WideOrbit', 'FreeWheel', 'Operative.One', 'Nielsen Avails'). Used for avails integration and inventory management workflows.

Frequency at which invoices are generated for orders transacted through this sales channel: weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly, upon_delivery (post-air billing), or upon_execution (pre-pay/upfront). Drives billing cycle configuration in the OMS and accounts receivable.

Media category served by this sales channel, indicating the inventory type sold through it: linear_tv (broadcast/cable), streaming (OTT/AVOD/FAST), digital (display/video online), radio, out_of_home, print, or multiplatform (cross-platform bundles). Used for revenue segmentation and audience reporting.

Short, externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the sales channel (e.g., DIRECT, AGENCY, PROG, BARTER). Used as a stable business key in downstream joins and Salesforce Media Cloud picklist values. Referenced by sales_channel_ref_id across the sales domain.
Human-readable full name of the sales channel (e.g., 'Direct Sales', 'Agency / Rep Firm', 'Programmatic', 'Barter/Trade'). Displayed in reports, dashboards, and Salesforce opportunity records.

Current lifecycle status of the sales channel record: active (available for use in proposals and orders), inactive (temporarily disabled), deprecated (retired, no new business), or pilot (in limited trial). Controls availability in Salesforce picklists and rate card assignments.

Broad classification of the sales channel by commercial model: direct (sold by internal sales team), agency (sold through ad agency or rep firm), programmatic (automated/algorithmic buying), barter (trade/exchange deals), self_serve (advertiser-direct digital portal), or partner (reseller/affiliate). Drives commission structures and revenue recognition rules.

Indicates whether this channel primarily airs children's programming subject to COPPA and FCC Children's Television Act restrictions (True). Restricts certain ad categories and data collection practices on this channel.

Maximum content rating permitted for advertising or content sold/distributed through this channel, based on TV Parental Guidelines or MPAA ratings (e.g., TV-G, TV-PG, TV-14, TV-MA). Enforces brand safety and regulatory compliance for ad placement.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary country in which this sales channel operates (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR', 'CAN'). Used for international revenue segmentation, regulatory compliance, and multi-territory deal management.

Standard payment credit terms in calendar days applicable to invoices generated from orders on this sales channel (e.g., 30 = Net 30, 45 = Net 45). Used by billing to set invoice due dates and aging buckets.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the primary currency in which deals are transacted through this sales channel (e.g., 'USD', 'GBP', 'EUR'). Supports multi-currency operations for international distribution and licensing channels.

Comma-separated list or description of dayparts for which this sales channel is applicable (e.g., 'Primetime, Late Night, Daytime'). Informs rate card applicability and scheduling constraints. Free-text to accommodate complex multi-daypart configurations.

Date after which this sales channel record is no longer valid for new business (yyyy-MM-dd). Null indicates an open-ended/indefinitely active channel. Used to retire deprecated channels while preserving historical order references.
Date from which this sales channel record is valid and available for use in proposals, orders, and rate cards (yyyy-MM-dd). Supports temporal validity management for channel lifecycle changes.

Indicates whether FCC broadcast licensing requirements apply to this sales channel (True for over-the-air broadcast channels, False for cable/streaming/digital channels). Drives compliance workflow routing for political advertising and equal opportunity rules.

tags: confidential
